Day One

KITCHEN NOTES / DAY ONE

The only 3 tools you actually need

You do not need a 12-piece knife block or copper pots. You need three things to make 90% of meals.

Knife → Board → Pan
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    A Chef's Knife

    An 8-inch chef's knife is all you need. Do not buy a set. Spend your budget on one good knife that feels comfortable to hold.

    Look for It should feel balanced in your hand, not too heavy.

  2. 02

    A Large Cutting Board

    A big wooden or plastic board. Small boards make chopping frustrating and dangerous because food rolls off.

    Look for The board should be wider than your knife.

  3. 03

    A 10-inch Skillet

    A non-stick or stainless steel skillet with a lid. It fries eggs, simmers sauces, and toasts nuts.

    Look for It should be large enough that food has space to breathe.

  4. 04

    Skip the gadgets

    Garlic presses, egg slicers, and avocado tools are unnecessary. Your knife does all of this.

    Look for A clean drawer with fewer tools is better than a cluttered one.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

You can cook an entire meal without reaching for a special gadget.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Buying a massive block of knives and tools you will never use.

More tools just mean more things to wash and lose track of.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Buy three high-quality essentials.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

Any heavy pan works if you do not have a skillet, but a skillet makes tossing and flipping much easier.

What about pots?

A medium pot for boiling pasta or rice is helpful, but if you only have a deep skillet, you can survive your first week.
